comments.author: the_zword
comments.body:
It was an interesting concept until I had to buy the dynamite.

Too many clicks, the popup breaks the engagement with demolition strategy, and the levels are still easy.

The game interface is forcing me to disengage with the core mechanic in order to support resource management as Im just starting to gain interest. Gotta push that out a few levels

comments.author: Bastion80
comments.body:
It’s because the game feels boring. I played 17 levels (so definitely more than 2 minutes), and every single one felt basically the same: place TNT on pillars and watch things collapse. It honestly felt like I was playing the same tutorial level 17 times with slightly different shapes.

The lack of creativity is kind of insane, honestly. The fun in a game like this should come from strategically placing explosives to solve unique situations and complete levels in clever ways.

Maybe it gets better later in the game, I don’t know… but after blowing up pillars 17 times in a row, I had enough.

replies.author: Clear-Reach8805
replies.body: The first version was really difficult, and I received a lot of negative feedback from players who couldn't get past level 3 because they couldn't identify the truly important points in the structure. I wasn't able to find a good balance between levels to work for both very smart and very "not-so-smart" players. But I'm working on it. Thank you for your valuable feedback.

replies.author: Bastion80
replies.body: I understand, what you think about adding maybe 2 difficulty levels? I know that it will be a lot of work but it's an idea. Easy-Medium-Hard.

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body: What's the point of you making a game? Place explosives, tower collapses. Then what? Do you know how to make games? I don't mean how to prompt. Do you know what is making games?

replies.author: Bastion80
replies.body: He said the game had bad feedback because it was to hard... now it is to easy. Yeah... making games is not easy but why attack him? If he want to make a game and share it who cares. Our feedback can help and who cares if he used visual-scripting, AI or written everything from scratch. We judge the outcome, not the development process.

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body: I'm not attacking him. I want to know if he knows anything about making games? If I tell you I want to become a chef, and I point at the soggy bread on the floor, will you attack me and ask me why there's soggy bread on the floor, instead of helping me achieve my dreams to become a chef?

comments.author: je386
comments.body:
As others stated, go on another platform. If you hadn't asked for feedback, I would not even have started the game. The menu looks like total slop games and not worth a look.

The game itself is nice. There could be a bit more different kind of challenges, but it is okay and I played through level 39.

You main problem is the platform. Potential players not even trying your game will not give it a chance.
